supplement.where: Appendices A-I are included on PDF pp. 27-84. Preregistration documents are described as online/OSF, but their URLs are removed to maintain anonymity (pp. 41, 43 and 66).
supplement.holds: Included appendices provide analyzed arm counts (Tables A.1-A.3, pp. 35-37), sample construction/exclusions (Appendix C.4-C.5, pp. 45-47), scoring details (Appendix D, pp. 49-52), participant-clustered inference and additional regression coefficients/SEs (Appendix F, pp. 55-59), the Revised-versus-DALL-E-2 logo CI (p. 58), Z-score/DreamSim robustness estimates and CIs (Appendix H, pp. 63-65), and fuller preregistered replication analyses/deviations (Appendix I, pp. 66-84). No numerical result recorded here depends on a separate unavailable statistical supplement.

paper_design_summary: Two preregistered online experiments assigned US Prolific participants to DALL-E 2, DALL-E 3 with attempted suppression of prompt rewriting, or DALL-E 3 with default GPT-4 rewriting. Participants iteratively reproduced a target image in the first experiment or designed an original logo from an open-ended brief in the second; image-target similarity and LLM-derived logo quality were scored, respectively. Researcher replay of the same prompts on alternative models separated model-capability and prompt-adaptation components (pp. 8-13, sections 3-3.4; pp. 40 and 43, participant recruitment; pp. 49-50, scoring).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Each participant was blindly assigned to an image-generation model configuration and a target item. Complete randomization jointly assigned three model configurations and fifteen target images or logo briefs, producing 45 model-by-task cells (p. 34, Appendix B.1).

participants.exclusions: The raw dataset contained 2,059 participants; this is a raw-data count, not an explicit tally at random assignment. Removing blank prompts, invalid Prolific IDs and logging failures left 2,029 people; requiring at least 10 successful prompts left 1,914. Restriction to the first 10 prompts was not preregistered. Excluding participants who repeated the same prompt at least five times consecutively left 1,899; excluding incomplete surveys left 1,893. Further post-hoc removal of prompts with failed image generation/replay or duplicate attempt numbers affected 370 prompts, leaving 18,560 prompts and the same 1,893 people. These are analysis counts after exclusions (pp. 45-46, Appendix C.4).
participants.who: US Prolific participants, fluent English speakers, using desktop or laptop devices; no prior generative-AI experience was required. Data collection: December 12-19, 2023 (p. 40, Appendix B.4.1-B.4.3).
participants.quote: Our final sample thus included 1,893 participants and 18,560 prompts.

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI DALL-E 2; DALL-E 3 (Verbatim); DALL-E 3 (Revised, with GPT-4 prompt rewriting)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants iteratively wrote their own prompts and inspected generated images in a custom interface. Each request was memoryless, although the interface displayed earlier prompts and outputs. Participants were blind to the model configuration and hidden prompt rewriting. The Verbatim arm attempted to suppress rewriting with a hidden instruction; the Revised arm retained default rewriting (p. 9, section 3.1; p. 38, Appendix B.2).

task.description: Iteratively prompt the assigned model to reproduce one randomly assigned target image as closely as possible. Fifteen targets covered business/marketing, graphic design, and architectural photography. This bounded target-matching task is retained in the study inventory but is not the open-ended creative task supporting core eligibility (pp. 8-11, sections 3-3.3).
task.duration: Up to 25 minutes to submit at least 10 prompts; analysis restricted to the first 10 prompts (p. 9, section 3.1; pp. 45-46, Appendix C.4).

outcomes.name: Image-to-target fidelity: expected CLIP cosine similarity
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity between the generated image and the fixed target, averaged over 10 generated images per prompt for the main analysis (pp. 10-11, section 3.2.1; p. 45, Appendix C.3). Higher means more faithful target replication, not greater originality or greater similarity across different participants. The analysis unit is a prompt-level expected image score, coded output; n_units is the retained prompt count across all three arms, not the count in any individual contrast (p. 46, Appendix C.4). Two-way fixed-effects models control target and attempt, with participant-clustered standard errors (p. 55, Appendix F.1.1; pp. 56-57, Appendix F.1.3). DreamSim, within-target/attempt Z scores and percentile rescalings are robustness variants of fidelity and are grouped here (p. 49, Appendix D.1; pp. 53-54, Appendix E.2; pp. 63-64, Appendix H.1-H.2). The Z-scored effect is the paper's rescaled output-level estimate, not a newly computed participant-level standardized mean difference. Initial/best-attempt analyses and performance-quantile analyses also concern this fidelity outcome, rather than creative diversity (p. 17, Table 1; Appendix I).
outcomes.delay: Human prompting occurred in the assisted task session. Main-text image scores use later researcher-generated replays/resamples of the same prompts; this is not a later unassisted participant test (p. 45, Appendix C.3).

contrasts.reported: ATE = 0.0164 higher CLIP cosine similarity, 95% CI [0.0104, 0.0224], p < 10^-5; approximately 0.19 standard deviations (p. 14). Z-score robustness: z = 0.19, 95% CI [0.100, 0.271] (p. 64). DreamSim robustness: delta = 0.0306, p < 10^-7; z = 0.238, 95% CI [0.152, 0.324] (p. 63). Replay decomposition of the same total gain: model effect = 0.0084, p < 10^-8, approximately 51%; prompting effect = 0.0079, p = 0.024, approximately 48% (p. 15). These decomposition estimates hold prompt content or replay model fixed and do not represent additional randomized participant arms.
contrasts.locator: p. 14, section 4.1.1 and Figure 1B; pp. 15-16, section 4.1.2 and Figure 2; p. 63, Appendix H.1.1; p. 64, Appendix H.2.1; p. 55, Appendix F.1.1 and pp. 56-57, Appendix F.1.3 (inference)

contrasts.reported: Delta = 0.0069 in CLIP cosine similarity; p = 0.042. A raw point estimate and p-value are printed; no numeric standard error or interval is supplied for this raw contrast here.

The paper reports the reverse orientation: automated prompt revision reduced the benefit of DALL-E 3 by 58% (95% CI [40%, 76%]). This is a relative reduction in the upgrade benefit, not an absolute CLIP difference. The printed percentage and interval are preserved without recomputing a Verbatim-minus-Revised effect.

task.description: Create the best original logo for a hypothetical organization from one randomly assigned brief. Fifteen briefs specified the organization, background, a few required visual elements, and intended uses, while allowing open-ended creative designs. There was no target image or uniquely optimal design (p. 11, section 3.3; p. 41, Appendix B.5.1-B.5.2).
task.duration: Up to 25 minutes to submit at least 10 prompts; analysis restricted to the first 10 prompts (p. 9, section 3.1; p. 41, Appendix B.5.1; p. 47, Appendix C.5).

outcomes.name: Logo design quality: Bradley-Terry strength
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The gpt-4.1-nano multimodal judge compared which of two logos better fulfilled the client's specific requirements; temperature was 0 and image order was randomized. Twenty percent of possible within-brief pairs, including original and replayed images, were sampled, and Bradley-Terry beta strengths were fitted by maximum likelihood (pp. 11-12, section 3.3.1; pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2). This rates design quality/appropriateness, not explicitly novelty or holistic creativity, so construct is usefulness. Scores and main regressions are at the individual logo/prompt level, not the pair or participant level. The n_units value is 18,425 retained original prompt/output records across all three arms; it is not a pair count or the full number of original-plus-replay images (p. 47, Appendix C.5). ATEs use attempt and brief fixed effects with participant-clustered standard errors (p. 58, Appendix F.2.1). Z-scored BT analyses are robustness variants of this outcome, grouped here; normalization follows the within-task/attempt procedure across model arms, not participant-level Cohen's d (pp. 53-54, Appendix E.2; pp. 64-65, Appendix H.3). Distributional analyses concern dispersion in quality, not similarity of design content (pp. 20-21, section 4.2.3 and Table 2). Human-rater benchmarking was attempted but the reported outcome relies on the LLM judge because human agreement was weak; the number of human evaluators is not stated (p. 12, footnote 9).
outcomes.delay: Participant outputs were produced during the AI-assisted session. Subsequent researcher replay and scoring do not constitute delayed unassisted creative work (pp. 12-13, sections 3.3.1-3.4; p. 45, Appendix C.3).

contrasts.reported: ATE = 0.8075 in Bradley-Terry beta, 95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], p < 10^-10; approximately 0.57 standard deviations (p. 18). Z-scored robustness: z = 0.569, 95% CI [0.502, 0.636], p < 10^-10 (p. 64). Replay decomposition of the same total gain: model effect = 0.748, p < 10^-10, approximately 92.7%; prompting effect = 0.0577, p = 0.101, 7.2% (p. 19). The model effect compares the same DALL-E 2 prompts across rendering models; the prompting effect compares DALL-E 3 and DALL-E 2 participants' prompts on DALL-E 3. These are decomposition analyses of the same sample, not new randomized participant arms.
contrasts.locator: p. 18, section 4.2.1 and Figure 3B; pp. 19-20, section 4.2.2 and Figure 4; p. 58, Appendix F.2.1; p. 59, Appendix F.2.3; pp. 64-65, Appendix H.3.1

The paper reports the reverse orientation, Revised relative to Verbatim: a 3.2% increase in BT beta on average, 95% CI [-5.6%, 12.1%]. The interval includes zero. The printed percentage and interval are preserved without calculating an absolute difference or a reversed percentage.

eligibility.reason: S2 supports core inclusion: individual participants were randomly assigned to different generative-AI configurations (p. 9, section 3.1; p. 34, Appendix B.1); 1,857 people were analyzed, with 628 DALL-E 2, 617 DALL-E 3 Verbatim and 612 DALL-E 3 Revised (p. 36, Table A.2; p. 47, Appendix C.5); and an open-ended original-logo task was evaluated on the resulting designs using automated comparative quality scores (pp. 11-12, sections 3.3-3.3.1; pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2). The outcome is coded usefulness because the judge assessed fulfillment of the client brief, within the codebook's quality/appropriateness category for creative design. All participants had generative AI, so the eligible contrast is ai_design, not AI versus no AI or AI versus human output. S1 is a bounded target-replication task; its fidelity outcome is retained with question none and is not the basis for core inclusion.

one_line_finding: In the logo experiment, DALL-E 3 Verbatim improved design quality over DALL-E 2 by 0.8075 Bradley-Terry beta (95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], p < 10^-10; p. 18, section 4.2.1), with replay attributing approximately 92.7% of the gain to the model and 7.2% to prompt adaptation (p. 19, section 4.2.2).
open_questions: Exact totals randomized before any attrition are not explicitly reported: 2,059 and 2,067 are raw-data contributor counts (pp. 45-46), and Table A.3's N = 1924 is an intermediate logo sample (pp. 37 and 46). Assignment counts are therefore null.

Preregistration URLs are redacted, preventing independent verification of any preregistered primary-outcome designation and planned analyses; the form records the manuscript's preregistration claim and paper-primary outcomes (pp. 41, 43 and 66).
notes: The entire markdown, including all appendices, was read; eligibility, counts, scoring and recorded estimates were checked using the PDF page text. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. The largest analyzed participant sample in one experiment is S1, whereas S2 supplies core creativity eligibility. The two outcome entries include one out-of-scope fidelity outcome for completeness. Prompt length, parts of speech, successive prompt similarity, within-user prompt dispersion and strategic shifts describe model inputs/interaction strategies rather than scored creative outputs, so they are not additional creative outcomes (Appendix D.3-D.8, pp. 50-52). Likewise, the performance-distribution analyses in Tables 1 and 2 do not measure content homogenization across people. There is no after_ai assessment: post-hoc replay renders existing prompts and is not a new participant task. Replay and robustness analyses reuse the two experimental samples and are not counted as new studies. For direct comparisons between DALL-E 3 configurations, Verbatim is the tested modification and Revised is the actual default; reported percentages are explicitly labeled in their original reverse orientation. No effect sizes, standard errors, confidence intervals or reversed percentages were calculated. Anonymized data and replication code are promised upon publication, but no usable URLs are supplied (p. 8, footnote 4).
